{"id": "53504ce2-c991-4444-bc09-4d09fba3b8da", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "Here's the thing: `0x80073712` is the single most misleading error code in Windows servicing, because **two completely different root causes produce it, and `DISM /RestoreHealth` only fixes one of them.** That's almost certainly why you're looping.

### Why your two RestoreHealth runs didn't converge

On Server 2016 specifically, cumulative updates ship as a **separate SSU + LCU pair** (unlike 2019+, which combines them). If the servicing stack is outdated, it literally can't parse the new LCU's manifest — and that failure *surfaces* as "component store corrupted," even though the store itself may be fine. Running `/RestoreHealth` against that doesn't touch the actual cause, so it loops.

### Correct order of operations (don't skip or reorder)

**1. Rule out a halted pending transaction first** — this alone can poison both SSU installs and RestoreHealth:
```powershell
DISM /Online /Get-Packages /Format:Table | Select-String "Pending"
Test-Path "$env:SystemRoot\servicing\Packages\pending.xml"
```
If pending packages or a *stale* (>24h) `pending.xml` show up:
```powershell
DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RevertPendingActions
```
Then reboot — some transactions only finalize at boot.

**2. Check whether the Servicing Stack Update is current** — this is almost certainly your real cause given the Installing-phase failure:
```powershell
$os = Get-CimInstance Win32_OperatingSystem
"$($os.Caption) Build $($os.BuildNumber).$((Get-ItemProperty 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion').UBR)"

$s = (New-Object -ComObject Microsoft.Update.Session).CreateUpdateSearcher().Search("IsInstalled=0 and Type='Software'").Updates
$s | ?{$_.Title -match 'Servicing Stack'} | %{ "SSU: $($_.Title)" }
```
If an SSU shows up as not-installed, install **that alone first** (via WU/WSUS or the Update Catalog), confirm it completes, then retry the LCU. SSUs are forward-only — they can't be uninstalled, but that's expected and fine.

**3. Only now re-run the store repair**, if corruption is still indicated:
```powershell
DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /StartComponentCleanup
DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /ScanHealth
DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth
sfc /scannow
```
If this instance is on an isolated/restricted-network fleet where Windows Update isn't reachable as a repair source, RestoreHealth will silently retry WU and time out — supply an explicit matching-build source instead: `/Source:WIM:<path>\install.wim:<idx> /LimitAccess`. The WIM build+UBR must match exactly or it fails generically.

**4. If WU components look implicated**, reset the datastore/catroot after the store is healthy:
```powershell
Stop-Service wuauserv,cryptSvc,bits,msiserver -Force
Rename-Item "$env:SystemRoot\SoftwareDistribution" "$env:SystemRoot\SoftwareDistribution.old" -Force
Rename-Item "$env:SystemRoot\System32\catroot2" "$env:SystemRoot\System32\catroot2.old" -Force
Start-Service wuauserv,cryptSvc,bits,msiserver
```

**5. Reboot**, then validate before re-attempting the patch:
```powershell
DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /CheckHealth   # must say healthy, not just RestoreHealth exit 0
```
Confirm no packages remain "Pending", no SSU remains in the `IsInstalled=0` search, `pending.xml` is gone, and `wuauserv` is running. Only then retry the cumulative update.

If you'd like, I can help you check this instance's current build/UBR and pending-update state directly via Systems Manager if it's SSM-managed — just share the instance ID and region.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
